lecture_context.lecture_title: What’s Going On Inside My Model?

unit.name: Occlusion sensitivity and class activation maps
unit.description: Shows two localization-oriented CNN interpretation methods: perturbing input regions and restructuring the classifier with global average pooling to produce class activation maps.
unit.summary: Occlusion sensitivity replaces a moving region of the image with a gray or dark square and measures how the true-class score changes as the square moves [ts=1524s] [ts=1557s]. If occluding the dog face drops the Pomeranian probability, or occluding a wheel drops the car-wheel probability, the method supports the claim that the model is relying on semantically relevant regions [ts=1608s] [ts=1657s]. The class activation map section targets real-time visualization: the lecture identifies fully connected layers after flattening as the part that mixes away localization, then replaces most of that head with global average pooling plus a final fully connected layer [ts=1725s] [ts=1834s] [ts=1893s]. A CAM is then formed as a weighted combination of last-convolution feature maps for a selected class, producing a heatmap that can be overlaid on the input [ts=1973s] [ts=2054s].

key_points.text: Occlusion sensitivity scans a mask over the image and records how the true-class score changes at each mask position.
A score drop when the square covers the object of interest suggests the model is using that region for the class decision.
Occluding a human face increased the Afghan-hound score in the example, implying the human face was distracting rather than helpful evidence.
Flattening followed by multiple fully connected layers mixes spatial information and makes localization harder.
Replacing flatten-plus-many-FC layers with global average pooling preserves a link between last convolutional maps and class scores.
A class activation map is a class-specific weighted combination of last-convolution feature maps.

kp_catalog.name: Occlusion sensitivity
kp_catalog.description: A perturbation-based CNN interpretation method that masks regions of the input and records changes in the class score.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The method is presented as intuitive and simple, with several examples showing whether true-class probability drops when key object regions are masked [ts=1524s] [ts=1608s].

kp_catalog.name: Class activation maps with global average pooling
kp_catalog.description: A CNN localization method that preserves spatial information by using global average pooling and class-specific weights over last-convolution feature maps.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: CAM is taught as a practical way to provide real-time localization by modifying the network architecture rather than running an expensive post-hoc scan [ts=1725s] [ts=1893s].
